title: Constant coefficient rings under scheme inverse image
statement: For every commutative topological ring B and scheme T, a monoidal isomorphism between the sheafified constant ULift B ring on profinite sets and its condensed continuous-function ring induces a monoidal isomorphism between the sheafified constant ULift B ring on T-pro-etale and the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. No finiteness, nonzero-ring or nonempty-scheme condition is required for this pullback step.

source.place: Section 5.3; uniqueness of monoidal left adjoints and the constant-sheaf adjunction

proof.text: Evaluation at a terminal object is right adjoint to the constant-sheaf functor. Pushforward composed with these sections is sections at the image terminal object. This natural isomorphism is monoidal.

Conjugate the monoidal sections comparison under the two constant-sheaf adjunctions and the inverse-image adjunction. Apply first to profiniteToProEt and then to the scheme structural map. The pullback of the terminal pro-etale object is terminal, by invertibility of its structural map.

Apply the resulting monoidal natural isomorphism to ULift B. Explicitly identify monoid structures for constant ring presheaves, sheafification, and composition, using monObjObj_comp. Map the given coefficient-ring isomorphism along upperStarFromPoint and compose the ring-object morphisms.

D3: terminal object and coefficient comparison are specified by proved equalities to their original explicit constructions. The chosen witnesses are unique by equality; no arbitrary existence data is used.

        (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B))) ≅ Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B)
    (heR : IsMonHom eR.hom) :

      ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} B))) ≅
        condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} B) T,
      IsMonHom e.hom
